frozen_source_lines.text: 5.1 Let $Z$ be a finite-dimensional Cartan-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module. Then $N\otimes Z$ is again a genuine parabolic object: its weights are sums of weights of $N$ and $Z$, and local finiteness for $\mathfrak p$ follows from $U(\mathfrak p)n\otimes Z$ being finite-dimensional for each $n$. It is finitely generated over $U(\mathfrak m)$ by tensors of generators of $N$ with a basis of $Z$: induction on word length uses $xn\otimes z=x(n\otimes z)-n\otimes xz$. Thus its $V$ image is defined on the stated domain. Apply the original-head right Skryabin counit $H_N\otimes_W Q_{\chi,\mathrm{right}}\to D_\chi N$, $f\otimes\overline a\mapsto fa$. Tensor it with $Z^\vee$, apply right Wh and use step 2.3 to obtain $H_N\circledast_{\mathrm{right}}Z^\vee\cong H_{N\otimes Z}$. Combine this actual counit with the module pairing of step 4.1 and take finite duals. This gives the natural $W$ isomorphism $\nu_{N,Z}:V(N\otimes Z)\to V(N)\circledast Z$ for EVERY genuine parabolic object $N$, including objects without an induced-module realization. Coassociativity, counit associativity and the inverse product formulas of step 3.2 make its two iterated tensor constructions agree under transported associativity. Naturality in a map of finite tensor factors follows from its ordinary dual map and the basis-independent evaluation pairing; hence adjacent flips are intertwined. [F2, F6, step 2.3, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

6.1 Compute the actual Casimir coefficients in ordinary box matrix units. On the LEFT lift, the coefficient at $v_k$ after $\Omega=\sum E_{ab}\otimes E_{ba}$ is $\sum_hE_{h,k}\eta_{\mathrm{tail}}X_{hj}$. Positive matrices give $(E_{h,k}-\delta_{hk}\rho_k^{\mathrm{tail}})X_{hj}$ after undoing the shift. Negative matrices give $\chi(E_{h,k})X_{hj}-X_{kj}$ by step 1.9. Their total scalar is $-\rho_k^{\mathrm{tail}}-\sum_{b>\operatorname{col}(k)}q_b=q_{\operatorname{col}(k)}-n$. On the RIGHT lift the coefficient at $v^h$ is $\sum_k\eta_{\mathrm{head}}Y_{ik}E_{h,k}$; step 2.2 moves negative matrices left, giving $\chi(E_{h,k})Y_{ik}-Y_{ih}$, and the total scalar is $-\rho_h^{\mathrm{head}}-\sum_{b<\operatorname{col}(h)}q_b=q_{\operatorname{col}(h)}-n$. Multiplying by $Y$ on the left or $X$ on the right therefore gives the SAME entries $C_{j,i}=\sum_{\operatorname{col}(h)\le\operatorname{col}(k)}Y_{i,k}E_{h,k}X_{h,j}+\sum_k(q_{\operatorname{col}(k)}-n)Y_{i,k}X_{k,j}+\sum_{\operatorname{row}(h)=\operatorname{row}(k),\,\operatorname{col}(h)=\operatorname{col}(k)-1}Y_{i,h}X_{k,j}$. There is no extra displacement sign on the ordinary $E_{h,k}$; signs are already in $X,Y$. The entries lie in $W$ because the Casimir preserves the actual Whittaker subspace. The module pairing now intertwines the two transported Casimirs, while the continuous tensor pairing transposes the source Casimir term by term. Hence $\nu$ intertwines the source and target Casimir maps. With flip compatibility this also intertwines their polynomial and generalized-eigenspace residue projections, with the usual contragredient retained for reverse translation. [F2, F3, F6, step 1.9, step 2.2, step 4.1, step 5.1, construct, algebra]

frozen_source_lines.text: **Given:** the Axiom of Choice; a coefficient field $k$; a smooth complex algebraic variety $M$ of pure dimension $d$ with its analytic topology; morphisms of complex algebraic varieties $q:A\to M$ and $u:B\to M$; the fiber product $T=A\times_MB$ with its projections $a:T\to A$, $b:T\to B$; the diagonal $\Delta:M\to M\times M$; the map $F=(q,u):A\times B\to M\times M$; and the closed embedding $\theta:T\hookrightarrow A\times B$ of the support, which realizes $T$ as $F^{-1}(\Delta(M))$. For the equivariant assertions, additionally impose the characteristic-zero, product-general-linear-group and equivariance hypotheses of [F3].

2.1 Pullback and cap product on arbitrary supports. Put $S=A\times B$. Proper base change along $F=(q,u)$ identifies $F^*\Delta_*k_M[-2d]$ with $\theta_*k_T[-2d]$, so $F^*g_\Delta$ gives $g_F:\theta_*k_T[-2d]\to k_S$. For a dualizing class $c:k_S\to\omega_S[-n]$, compose $c\circ g_F$ and use $\theta_*\dashv\theta^!$ and $\theta^!\omega_S=\omega_T$. The resulting map $k_T\to\omega_T[2d-n]$ is a Borel–Moore class of degree $n-2d$ on $T$. This defines the supported cap operation even if $T$ is singular or has excess dimension; no purity of $\theta$ is asserted. The external product uses $\omega_A\boxtimes\omega_B=\omega_S$: on the supplied finite local product cochain models, compact-support cochains tensor, and their finite-dimensional duals tensor as well, giving this canonical comparison and its restriction compatibility. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Comparison with the exchange mate. For a constructible $C$ on $M$, the mate is the adjoint of $b_!a^*q^!C\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}^{-1}}u^*q_!q^!C\xrightarrow{u^*\epsilon_q}u^*C$, where the arbitrary-map proper-support exchange of [F1] supplies $\mathrm{BC}:u^*q_!\xrightarrow{\sim}b_!a^*$ and $\epsilon_q$ is the exceptional counit. To identify its dualizing evaluation with step 2.1, factor $q$ as its graph $\Gamma_q:A\hookrightarrow A\times M$ followed by the second projection. The graph is the pullback of $\Delta$ along $(q,\operatorname{id}_M):A\times M\to M\times M$; its supported orientation map is that pullback of $g_\Delta$. Base change of the graph along $\operatorname{id}_A\times u$ is exactly $\theta$, so its supported orientation map after this second pullback is $g_F$. For the product projection, tensor–Hom evaluation with the relative dualizing factor $\omega_A$ computes the counit; this is the finite product cochain evaluation of step 2.1. Composing the graph counit and that evaluation gives $\epsilon_q$ by the composition-of-counits identity in [F1]. Cartesian pasting therefore makes its base-changed composite exactly $u^*\epsilon_q\circ\mathrm{BC}^{-1}$ above. Taking adjoints and using $q^!k_M=\omega_A[-2d]$ proves that the exchange, paired with the second dualizing class by tensor evaluation, is $c\circ g_F$ under $\theta_*\dashv\theta^!$. Every map retains support on $T$ throughout this factorization. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1]

frozen_source_lines.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited constructible and cellular suppliers. In
the point/projective-line geometry with $E=\mathrm{pt}$, $X_1=\mathrm{pt}$, $X_2=\mathbb P^1$,
$d_1=0$, $d_2=1$ and $L_1=k$, $L_2=R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]$ in the setting of
[[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], let
$\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{-1}(L_1,L_2)$ be the unit $k\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$ and let
$\beta\in\operatorname{Ext}^{1}(L_2,L_1)$ be point evaluation
$R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]\to k[1]$, that is, evaluation $H^0(\mathbb P^1,k)\to k$ shifted by
$1$ and extended by zero on $H^2$. Then
$\alpha*\beta=\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$ in the source-first convention of
[[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], and under the
correspondence isomorphism of
[[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] one has
$[\mathbb P^1]*[\mathrm{pt}]=[\mathrm{pt}]$: the refined diagonal intersection of the fundamental
class of $\mathbb P^1$ with the point class is the point class, and proper pushforward to the
point corner gives its generator.

1.1 The geometry and the cohomology of the projective line. The fiber products are $Z_{12}=Z_{21}=\mathbb P^1$. By [F3] its Schubert CW structure has one $0$-cell and one $2$-cell, so the cellular cochain complex is $k\oplus k[-2]$. By [F4] it computes singular cohomology, and [F6] identifies this with constant-sheaf cohomology. Choosing cocycles representing the two generators gives a quasi-isomorphism $k\oplus k[-2]\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$. Hence $L_2\simeq k[1]\oplus k[-1]$ and $L_1=k$. [F3, F4, F6, algebra]

2.1 The two classes and their composites. The unit $\alpha:k\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$ includes the degree-zero summand, generating $\operatorname{Ext}^{-1}(L_1,L_2)=k$. Evaluation at a point projects to that summand; its shift $\beta:L_2\to k[1]$ generates $\operatorname{Ext}^1(L_2,L_1)=k$, since $\operatorname{Hom}(k[-2],k)=0$. Therefore $\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$. The reverse composite $\alpha[1]\circ\beta$ is also nonzero: it is the projector of $L_2=k[1]\oplus k[-1]$ onto $k[1]$, and is neither zero nor $\operatorname{id}_{L_2}$. [step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The convolution check. Apply [F2] with $(i,j,k)=(1,2,1)$ and degrees $r=-1$, $s=1$ to the composable pair $\alpha:L_1\to L_2[r]$ and $\beta:L_2\to L_1[s]$: since $\beta[r]\circ\alpha=\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$ by step 2.1, the product theorem gives $\Phi_{11}^{0}(\operatorname{id}_k)=\Phi_{12}^{-1}(\alpha)*\Phi_{21}^{1}(\beta)$, so $\alpha*\beta=\operatorname{id}_k$ in the source-first convention, and the right-hand side is the convolution product of [F1]. The corner degrees are $d_1+d_2-r=2$ for $\alpha$ and $d_2+d_1-s=0$ for $\beta$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 The geometric product. The adjunction chain of [F1] sends $\alpha$ to $\operatorname{id}_{k_{\mathbb P^1}}$, hence to the positive fundamental class $[\mathbb P^1]$. Write $i:\mathrm{pt}\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^1$ for the evaluation point. Evaluation is the global-sections image of $k_{\mathbb P^1}\to i_*k$, and its adjoint under $R\Gamma\dashv a^!$, $a:\mathbb P^1\to\mathrm{pt}$, is the composite $k_{\mathbb P^1}\to i_*k=i_*i^!\omega_{\mathbb P^1}\to\omega_{\mathbb P^1}$, with the last arrow the proper trace. Thus $\Phi_{21}^{1}(\beta)=i_*[\mathrm{pt}]$ with coefficient $+1$. Geometrically $\mathbb P^1\times\{i\}$ meets the middle diagonal of $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ transversely at $(i,i)$; the map from its tangent line to the complex normal line of the diagonal is an isomorphism, preserving the real orientation. The positive Thom cap of [F5] therefore gives that point with multiplicity $+1$, and proper pushforward to $Z_{11}=\mathrm{pt}$ gives $[\mathrm{pt}]$. This computes $[\mathbb P^1]*[\mathrm{pt}]=[\mathrm{pt}]$, with middle degree drop $2$ and no permutation sign, agreeing with step 3.1. It verifies a transverse instance of the calculus, not its general nontransverse case. AC is inherited through [A1]. [A1, F1, F2, F5, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎
